design_detail: Regulatory briefing document, not a study: the background package (83 printed pages) written by the review staff of the US Food and Drug Administration (Division of Psychiatry, Office of Neuroscience, with tables credited to the clinical reviewer, the statistical reviewer and analyst, the Cardiac Safety Interdisciplinary Review Team and the epidemiology and risk-management reviewers) for the members of the Psychopharmacologic Drugs Advisory Committee before its meeting of 4 June 2024 on new drug application 215455, midomafetamine (MDMA) capsules with a psychological intervention for PTSD, submitted by Lykos Therapeutics on 11 December 2023. Its stated purpose is to obtain the committee's views on issues the Agency selected; its disclaimer says the conclusions are those of individual reviewers, not the Agency's final position, and that the package may not include every issue relevant to the decision. It contains: the regulatory history from 2001 to 2023; descriptions of the four 18-week studies (MAPP1, MAPP2, the open-label MP16 and the open-label extension MAPPUSX) and of the observational follow-up MPLONG; efficacy results re-tabulated from the sponsor's clinical study reports; safety results (deaths and serious adverse events across the programme, a pooled MAPP1 and MAPP2 adverse-event table, vital signs); a review of abuse-potential data; the FDA's own epidemiological analyses of illicit MDMA use; the proposed risk evaluation and mitigation strategy (REMS); and a pre-decisional benefit-risk framework. Read with its erratum (fda_2024b; card sc_fda_2024b), which corrects 29 passages. Analyses and data in this document that are not in the published trial reports (Mitchell et al., 2021, 2023): (1) the long-term follow-up MPLONG, analysed by the FDA separately for each trial (Table 8, Figure 3), with the FDA's comparison of people who did and did not enrol (Table 7), the interim treatments people received, an exploratory analysis by follow-up interval and the FDA's tipping-point analysis for interim use of ketamine, 5-MeO-DMT or MDMA obtained outside the study (Tables 16 and 17); (2) a pooled MAPP1 and MAPP2 adverse-event table regenerated by the FDA from the adverse-event dataset, with jaw-related events grouped apart from other muscle tightness (Table 13); (3) the Cardiac Safety team's outlier analysis of blood pressure and heart rate (Table 14, Figure 4); (4) serious adverse events and discontinuations across the whole development programme (Tables 10 to 12); (5) the analysis populations, including 91 randomized in MAPP1 (Table 3); (6) the MAPP2 blinding survey by degree of certainty (Table 9, from the MAPP2 clinical study report); (7) the regulatory record of the blinding disagreement (2016), the special protocol assessment letters (2017) with the instruction that abuse-related adverse events be documented, and the protocol amendments; (8) what the application lacked: positive or neutral drug effects not recorded as adverse events, no laboratory tests on dosing days in phase 3, no scheduled post-dose ECGs, an incomplete QT assessment; (9) abuse-related terms recorded in MAPPUSX from February 2023 (Table 15); (10) the FDA's independent analyses of ten surveillance data sources and a scoping review of the literature on illicit MDMA (Tables 18 to 23). Read in full from the PDF (text layer, all 83 pages); the pages with Tables 2 to 6, 8, 9, 13, 14 and 16 and Figures 1 to 4 were rendered and checked; figure values were not extracted except numbers printed on the figures.
can_establish: What the FDA's reviewers reported to the advisory committee before the vote: their reading of the two phase 3 trials and of the follow-up, their own re-analyses of the sponsor's data, what the application did and did not contain, the regulatory history, and the safety concerns they put to the committee.
cannot_establish: The FDA's final decision or its reasons (the document is pre-decisional and precedes the August 2024 action); whether the analyses reproduce the sponsor's raw data independently of the sponsor's datasets; the size of any expectancy or unblinding bias, which the reviewers say cannot be quantified; anything about the conduct of individual sites (site MP4 and the ethical violation behind the 2024 retractions are not mentioned).

sample.recruitment: Not applicable (regulatory briefing). The trial populations are re-reported from the sponsor's clinical study reports; recruitment methods are not described.
sample.inclusion_exclusion: As summarized by the FDA (pp. 18-19, with the erratum): DSM-5 PTSD for at least 6 months; MAPP1 PCL-5 of 46 or more at screening and CAPS-5 of 35 or more at baseline, MAPP2 PCL-5 of 40 or more and CAPS-5 of 28 or more. Excluded: psychotic disorder, bipolar I or dissociative identity disorder, current personality disorder, major depression with psychotic features, eating disorder with purging; moderate or severe alcohol or cannabis use disorder within set periods; any other substance use disorder in the past 12 months; current serious suicide risk (past attempts allowed); ongoing psychiatric medication; uncontrolled hypertension, arrhythmias, QTc above 450 ms (men) or 460 ms (women); liver disease; past hyponatremia or hyperthermia; ketamine within 12 weeks; ecstasy used more than 10 times in 10 years or within 6 months of the first session; earlier MAPS-sponsored MDMA trials; compensation litigation (the last three printed as MAPP2-only criteria, a restriction the erratum deletes).
sample.demographics: Table 4 (safety sets): women 27 of 46 (58.7%) on MDMA vs 32 of 44 (72.7%) on placebo in MAPP1 and 32 of 53 (60.4%) vs 42 of 51 (82.4%) in MAPP2; mean age 43.6 vs 38.2 (MAPP1) and 38.2 vs 40.0 (MAPP2); White 84.8% vs 68.2% and 69.8% vs 62.7%; Hispanic or Latino 10.9% vs 6.8% and 32.1% vs 21.6%; baseline CAPS-5 44.0 vs 44.2 and 39.4 vs 38.7.
sample.attrition: Table 3: MAPP1 91 randomized (46 MDMA, 45 placebo), 90 treated, 79 completed visit 19 (42 and 37); MAPP2 104 randomized (53 and 51), all treated, 103 in the mITT set, 96 completed visit 19 (53 and 43). MPLONG: 60 of MAPP1 and 82 of MAPP2 participants enrolled; 56 and 81 contributed an assessment (62% and 78% of those randomized).
sample.selection_effects: Two layers. The document's own selection: the FDA chose the issues to put to the committee and says the package may omit issues relevant to the final decision. The data's selection: MPLONG enrolment was voluntary, people who enrolled had lower CAPS-5 scores at the end of the trials than those who did not (20.2 vs 30.9), and enrolment differed by arm in MAPP2 (84.9% of the MDMA arm, 72.5% of the placebo arm); placebo participants could cross over to open-label MDMA in MAPPUSX (85 enrolled), and data after crossover were excluded.

exposure.measurement: MDMA (midomafetamine) capsules given only in supervised medication sessions of about 8 hours, three sessions 3 to 5 weeks apart, with three preparatory and nine integrative psychotherapy sessions; inactive placebo with the same psychotherapy as comparator.
exposure.dose_frequency_duration_route: Trial conditions as tabulated by the FDA (Table 2, p. 21): oral; session 1 an initial 68 mg and a further 34 mg 1.5 to 2 hours later if tolerated (102 mg), sessions 2 and 3 an initial 100 mg and a further 50 mg (150 mg), at least 21 days apart; 402 mg in total over the course. Low-dose MDMA comparators considered earlier in the programme were 25 or 30 mg (p. 35). Reported here only as the trials' conditions.
exposure.polysubstance: Psychoactive medicines not approved by the research team were prohibited from baseline to study termination (gabapentin and three opioids allowed for pain); marijuana and serotonergic herbs prohibited; antidepressant use after the first session meant stopping study treatment. Between the trials and the MPLONG visit, some participants used ketamine, 5-MeO-DMT, other psychedelics or MDMA obtained outside the study (p. 31).
exposure.abstinence_at_testing: Not applicable; a drug screen was part of the screening laboratory file (p. 49).

comparison.controls: Inactive placebo with identical psychotherapy. The FDA had asked in 2016 for a plan to mask placebo, suggesting niacin or low-dose MDMA; the sponsor preferred inert placebo, and the two did not agree at that meeting (pp. 12-13). No trial had an MDMA-only, placebo-only or psychotherapy-only arm (p. 17).
comparison.unmeasured_premorbid: Expectancy was not measured; lifetime MDMA use is not tabulated in this document.
comparison.controls_other_drug_use: Same exclusions as the MDMA arm; 7 placebo-arm participants reported MDMA use outside the study before the follow-up visit, against 13 from the MDMA arms (p. 31).

outcomes.instruments: CAPS-5 total severity (primary; 0 to 80, the sum of the first 20 of 30 items per the erratum), Sheehan Disability Scale (key secondary), PCL-5 (screening and MAPPUSX), adverse events coded to MedDRA, vital signs, C-SSRS. No laboratory tests on dosing days and no scheduled post-dose ECGs in phase 3.
outcomes.validity_norms: The FDA accepts a CAPS-5 change of 10 points or more as clinically meaningful and as the response threshold (pp. 13, 34; Varker et al., 2020).
outcomes.operationalization: Response: a fall of 10 points or more in CAPS-5; loss of diagnosis: response plus no longer meeting criteria; remission: no longer meeting criteria and CAPS-5 of 11 or less (p. 13). Treatment-emergent adverse events counted from the first medication session to study termination (Table 13 footnote); effects judged neutral, positive or favourable were not collected as adverse events (p. 50).
outcomes.multiplicity_correction: Hierarchical testing of CAPS-5 then SDS in each trial (p. 22); MPLONG analyses had no prespecified error control and are exploratory (p. 24); the FDA's epidemiological comparisons are descriptive, without formal tests (pp. 73-74).
outcomes.assessor_blinding: CAPS-5 and SDS by blinded, centralized independent raters by telemedicine, recordings used for inter-rater reliability (p. 19). The FDA judges that the in-session monitors could probably deduce allocation from behaviour during sessions (p. 9); assessors' guesses are not reported.

analysis.effect_sizes: Primary (Table 5): MAPP1 placebo-subtracted difference -11.86 (95% CI -17.41 to -6.32), P < 0.0001; MAPP2 -8.91 (-13.70 to -4.12), P = 0.0004. SDS (Table 6): -1.36 (-2.46 to -0.25), P = 0.0167, and -1.20 (-2.26 to -0.14), P = 0.0271. MPLONG (Table 8, p. 66): between-arm differences of -14.7 (MAPP1) and -11.96 (MAPP2) at the follow-up visit, no interval reported. Vital signs (Table 14): systolic pressure of 180 mm Hg or more in 6 of 99 vs 0 of 95, risk difference 6.1 (1.4 to 10.8).
analysis.covariates: Primary MMRM: baseline CAPS-5, dissociative subtype and site; MPLONG MMRM adds study and visit (pp. 23-25).
analysis.preregistration_detail: The FDA's own analyses (separate MPLONG models per trial, the time-window analysis, the tipping-point analysis for interim drug use, the vital-sign outlier analysis, the pooled adverse-event table) were not prespecified. The trials' primary analyses were agreed under a special protocol assessment (28 July 2017), with one deviation the FDA notes: Satterthwaite degrees of freedom were prespecified and the between-within method used, which made no practical difference (p. 23).
analysis.selective_reporting: The FDA notes the sponsor's literature searches were not exhaustive on arrhythmias (p. 46) and had gaps on harms of illicit MDMA (p. 60), and that positive or neutral effects were not recorded (p. 50). The document itself omits the trial-level breakdown of the pooled adverse events and does not mention site MP4.
analysis.power: Unblinded sample-size re-estimation at 60% completion in each trial; the data monitoring committee recommended no increase (p. 23).

interpretation_gap.results_show: Two trials with statistically significant CAPS-5 differences at 18 weeks; near-complete functional unblinding in MAPP2 (94% of the MDMA arm, 75% of the placebo arm guessed right) with the in-session monitors probably aware too; an uncontrolled single follow-up visit in 70% of those randomized, confounded by self-selection, unblinding and interim treatments; no data separating MDMA from the psychotherapy; adverse-event collection that left out positive drug effects; no laboratory, post-dose ECG or full QT data.
interpretation_gap.claimed: The executive summary describes "rapid, clinically meaningful, durable improvement" (p. 8) and improvement that appears durable for at least several months (p. 10); the detailed sections find the follow-up not designed to evaluate durability and its results of very limited value (p. 29), and the benefit-risk framework makes effectiveness conditional on the results being taken at face value (p. 65). The summary language is kinder to durability than the analysis behind it; the reviewers state the caveats in the same document.

timeline.event: The sponsor opens its investigational new drug application for MDMA in PTSD (p. 12).
End-of-phase-2 meeting: the FDA doubts the adequacy of blinding with inert placebo and suggests niacin or low-dose MDMA; no agreement (pp. 12-13).

Special protocol assessment: no-agreement letter (9 March), with the instruction that abuse-related adverse events be documented; Type A meeting (11 May); agreement letter (28 July); Breakthrough Therapy designation (15 August) (pp. 13-14).
MAPP1 protocol amendments on abuse-related events and suicide-risk events (16 September, 15 November) (p. 14).
MAPP1 completed (21 August); the FDA suggests a participant blinding survey for MAPP2 (19 October) (pp. 14, 16).
First phase 3 trial published (Mitchell et al., 2021); MPLONG starts in March (p. 37).
MAPP2 completed (2 November); Type B meeting on the safety database and durability (14 September) (pp. 15-16).

Second phase 3 trial published (Mitchell et al., 2023); positive drug effects first recorded, in MAPPUSX (February or March); MPLONG completed (21 May); application submitted (11 December) (pp. 15, 17, 50, 56).
This briefing document, with its erratum, for the advisory committee meeting of 4 June 2024.
Advisory committee votes 9 to 2 that the data do not show effectiveness and 10 to 1 that benefits do not outweigh risks (final summary minutes).
The FDA declines to approve the application in August, as reported by The BMJ (Mahase, 2024).

replication.where_it_stands: The document is the regulator's pre-decisional account; the sponsor's own briefing document for the same meeting (lykos_2024) is read by another reader. The FDA's decision letter is not among the documents read. The committee's votes and reasons are recorded in the final summary minutes (fda_2024c).

funding.funder: US Food and Drug Administration (government regulator); no external funding.
funding.affiliations_note: No individual authors are named; the FDA presenters at the meeting are listed in the minutes (fda_2024c, p. 4).

what_would_settle_it: For the questions the FDA raised: a trial whose comparator mimics MDMA's noticeable effects, or a factorial design with and without psychotherapy, with expectancy measured, all adverse events recorded including positive ones, laboratory tests and post-dose ECGs on dosing days, and randomized, prespecified follow-up of at least 6 to 12 months; for the record, the FDA's final review and decision letter.

domains.note: The data sources are named (clinical study reports, datasets, submissions) and the literature review on illicit MDMA is systematic (two databases, two screeners, 4,273 records); but the issues are chosen by the Agency for discussion and the disclaimer says relevant issues may be missing.
The trials and the follow-up are appraised in detail, with the reviewers' own re-analyses and sensitivity analyses.

domains.domain: Reliance on the authors' own studies
domains.note: The reviewers appraise the sponsor's studies; their own analyses are of the sponsor's data and of public surveillance sources.

Judgments are mostly labelled as such, but summary passages call the improvement durable while the detailed analysis finds the follow-up unable to show it, and the document reports the same survey result three ways and contains several internal inconsistencies (reporting issues).

domains.domain: Balance of benefits and risks (the sponsor's responses to the concerns are under-represented here; they are in its own briefing document)
domains.note: Positive results and limitations are both set out, including the arguments that durability might indicate a true drug effect.

risk_of_bias.reasoning: No validated instrument applies to a regulator's briefing document (METHODS §5.3); the editors' narrative-review checklist is used, its domains read as questions about the document as a source. The document may be cited, with page numbers, for what the FDA's reviewers reported and analysed before the advisory committee, for the regulatory history it records and for what the application lacked; its trial numbers come from the sponsor's study reports and datasets. It may not be cited for the FDA's final decision or reasons, and its own analyses of the follow-up are exploratory.

key_findings.finding: Background package prepared by the FDA for the committee; its conclusions are those of individual reviewers, not the final position of the reviewers, the division or the office; it focuses on issues the Agency identified and may not include every issue relevant to the final decision, which awaits the committee's input and the completed reviews.
key_findings.locator: Disclaimer statement

key_findings.finding: Because of MDMA's effects the studies are "nearly impossible to blind": per a post-study survey about 90% of those given the drug and 75% of those given placebo guessed their assignment; the in-session monitors could probably tell assignment from participants' behaviour, so participants and staff were both likely to know; the reviewers take it as a reasonable assumption that both biases influenced the observed treatment effects to some degree.
key_findings.locator: Executive Summary › Brief Description of Issues for Discussion at the AC, 1st paragraph
key_findings.note: The same survey is reported as 94% on p. 36 and as around 80 to 90% on p. 66; Table 9 gives 49 of 52 (94.2%). See reporting issue 1.

key_findings.finding: Because unblinding cannot be quantified, durability is considered as further evidence: at a follow-up 6 months to more than 2 years after treatment the MDMA arm's mean change remained greater than placebo, with some modest further improvement; about 25% dropped out between the trials and the follow-up, follow-up times varied and some participants had other treatments in the interval, which limits interpretation; how long unblinding and expectation effects last is unclear.
key_findings.locator: Executive Summary › Brief Description of Issues for Discussion at the AC, 2nd paragraph

key_findings.finding: The contribution of psychotherapy has not been characterized: every arm of every study included it, and no rigorous study compares this manualized therapy with other psychotherapies or with MDMA given without psychotherapy.
key_findings.locator: Executive Summary › Brief Description of Issues for Discussion at the AC, 3rd paragraph

key_findings.finding: Cardiac safety is not well characterized and the QT assessment is incomplete; rises in blood pressure and pulse were adverse events of special interest. Liver function was tested before and after dosing in one phase 1 and two phase 2 studies only, not in phase 3; hepatotoxicity was made an event of special interest only in the application, from literature on illicit use.
key_findings.locator: Executive Summary › Brief Description of Issues for Discussion at the AC, 4th and 5th paragraphs

key_findings.finding: Although the FDA had advised the sponsor to collect adverse events associated with abuse, the studies did not capture effects deemed positive, favourable or neutral, such as euphoria or elated mood; the application has no verbatim terms from participants and does not capture the onset or duration of the acute effects, which limits both the abuse-potential assessment and advice on monitoring.
key_findings.locator: Executive Summary › Brief Description of Issues for Discussion at the AC, 6th paragraph

key_findings.finding: On the positive side, the reviewers count two positive trials in which PTSD improved significantly and to a clinically meaningful degree on MDMA, an improvement that seems to last for at least several months without further doses; the committee is asked to weigh this against the uncertainties.
key_findings.locator: Executive Summary › Brief Description of Issues for Discussion at the AC, 8th paragraph

key_findings.finding: At the 2016 end-of-phase-2 meeting the FDA expressed concern about blinding and asked for a plan to mask placebo, suggesting niacin or low-dose MDMA; the sponsor argued that low doses had worsened anxiety in a few earlier participants and that niacin or other stimulants could worsen PTSD, and preferred inert placebo; the two did not agree on the adequacy of the blind.
key_findings.locator: Pertinent Drug Development and Regulatory History › Highlights of Regulatory History, 2nd paragraph

key_findings.finding: The special protocol assessment no-agreement letter of 9 March 2017 accepted a blinded centralized independent rater pool by live video and inactive placebo with identical psychotherapy, while stating continued concern about the adequacy of the blind; it agreed definitions of response (a CAPS-5 fall of 10 points or more), loss of diagnosis and remission (CAPS-5 of 11 or less), and advised that adverse events associated with potential abuse or overdose must be documented in all phase 1, 2 and 3 studies.
key_findings.locator: Highlights of Regulatory History, 3rd paragraph and its bullets; 4th paragraph

key_findings.finding: Type A meeting of 11 May 2017: two phase 3 trials of identical design, run independently and sequentially, mostly at the same sites; a thorough QT study to be done before the application; no new animal or human abuse-potential studies needed. Special protocol agreement letter 28 July 2017; Breakthrough Therapy designation 15 August 2017.
key_findings.locator: Highlights of Regulatory History, 5th to 7th paragraphs

key_findings.finding: MAPP1 amendments: in March 2018 a sub-study of sessions without an overnight stay (a support person stayed with the participant); in September 2019 nonpostural syncope added as an event of special interest, and all events related to drug abuse, intentional misuse, dependence, overdose or diversion to be captured as adverse events, but only those related to MDMA or ecstasy classed as events of special interest; in November 2019 suicide-risk events of special interest defined, including C-SSRS scores of 4 or 5.
key_findings.locator: Highlights of Regulatory History, 8th to 10th paragraphs

key_findings.finding: The participant blinding survey was suggested by the FDA on 19 October 2020, in response to a MAPP2 protocol amendment; MAPP1 had been completed on 21 August 2020 (Table 1), so only MAPP2 has the survey.
key_findings.locator: Highlights of Regulatory History, 11th paragraph (p. 14); Table 1 (p. 16); Efficacy Issue #1, 5th paragraph (p. 35)

key_findings.finding: At a Type B meeting on 14 September 2022 the FDA raised ongoing concerns about the adequacy of the safety database and the need for more data on durability, and about whether MPLONG could support durability, but agreed its results could be submitted. The application was submitted on 11 December 2023 with a hepatotoxicity signal report noting that most sponsor trials did not capture the relevant laboratory data.
key_findings.locator: Highlights of Regulatory History, 12th to 14th paragraphs

key_findings.finding: Efficacy data: MP16 (open-label phase 2, 33 enrolled), MAPP1 (91 randomized, completed 21 August 2020), MAPP2 (104 randomized, completed 2 November 2022), MAPPUSX (open-label extension for people from the placebo arms or without study drug, 85 enrolled, 78 completed); neither open-label study was meant to provide substantial evidence of effectiveness. MPLONG: one visit at least 6 months after the parent study; MAPP1 participants were told their allocation before enrolling, MAPP2 participants were not; completed 21 May 2023; 164 enrolled, 142 from MAPP1 and MAPP2.
key_findings.locator: Sources of Data for Efficacy; Table 1 (p. 16); Observational Study (pp. 16-17)

key_findings.finding: No study had an arm with MDMA or placebo without the psychological intervention, or the intervention alone. The integrative sessions, where most psychotherapeutic work appeared to occur, were not standardized in the treatment manuals and were left mainly to the individual therapist.
key_findings.locator: 3.1.2.1.1 Study Design, 3rd paragraph; Approach to Psychotherapy, 4th paragraph

key_findings.finding: The exclusion of people who had used ecstasy more than 10 times in 10 years or within 6 months of the first session, or who had been in an earlier MAPS MDMA trial, and of people in compensation litigation, is printed under a heading restricting it to MAPP2; the erratum deletes that heading.
key_findings.locator: 3.1.2.1.2 Study Population, paragraph after the last bullet; erratum item 2 (fda_2024b, p. 1)

key_findings.finding: Primary and key secondary outcomes were rated by blinded, centralized independent raters by telemedicine, trained and monitored, with recordings used for inter-rater reliability. The SDS is described as three items scored 0 to 10, summed to a total of 0 to 30; at the FDA's request, inability to work because of PTSD was scored 10 rather than missing.
key_findings.locator: 3.1.2.1.3 Efficacy Assessments; Sheehan Disability Scale (SDS)
key_findings.note: Table 6 (p. 29) prints SDS means of 6.0 to 7.4 at baseline, which fit a 0 to 10 metric rather than the 0 to 30 total described; see reporting issue 5.

key_findings.finding: The mITT set comprised randomized participants given study drug in at least one blinded session with at least one later CAPS-5; the primary de jure estimand excluded data after early termination and imputed nothing; CAPS-5 then SDS were tested hierarchically at a two-sided alpha of 0.0499, the remaining 0.0001 having been allocated to an unblinded sample-size re-estimation at 60% completion, after which the data monitoring committee recommended no increase.
key_findings.locator: 3.1.2.1.6 Statistical Analysis Methods; Sample Size Re-estimation; Analysis of the Primary Endpoint

key_findings.finding: MPLONG was an observational, noninterventional single visit at least 6 months after the last dose (in practice 6 months to more than 2 years); some participants had interim psychotherapy, ketamine, 5-MeO-DMT, MDMA from outside the study or other psychedelics; the effectiveness set excluded data after placebo participants joined MAPPUSX; the sponsor prespecified no error control or estimand, so the results are exploratory; the FDA analysed each trial separately because MAPP1 participants were unblinded and the severities differed.
key_findings.locator: 3.1.2.2 Observational Study MPLONG › Study Design; Statistical Analysis Methods; Analysis of the CAPS-5 Total Severity Score
key_findings.note: As corrected by the erratum (items 7 and 8), MPLONG enrolled people given drug or placebo, and its protocol included a review of medical history, not of adverse events.

key_findings.finding: Analysis populations: MAPP1 345 screened, 91 randomized (46 MDMA, 45 placebo), 90 in the safety and mITT sets (46 and 44), 79 per protocol, 79 completing visit 19 (42 and 37); MAPP2 324 screened, 104 randomized (53 and 51), 104 safety, 103 mITT (53 and 50), 94 per protocol, 96 completing visit 19 (53 and 43). MPLONG: enrolled 30 and 30 (MAPP1), 45 and 37 (MAPP2); effectiveness subset 27 and 29, 44 and 37.
key_findings.locator: Table 3
key_findings.note: The published report and the claims count MAPP1's 90 treated participants; one placebo participant was randomized but not treated.

key_findings.finding: Primary endpoint (de jure, mITT): MAPP1 least-squares mean change -24.50 (95% CI -28.28 to -20.71) on MDMA vs -12.64 (-16.61 to -8.66), difference -11.86 (-17.41 to -6.32), P < 0.0001, raw visit-19 means 19.5 vs 29.8 (n 42 and 37); MAPP2 -23.69 (-26.94 to -20.44) vs -14.78 (-18.28 to -11.28), difference -8.91 (-13.70 to -4.12), P = 0.0004, raw means 15.8 vs 23.3 (n 52 and 42). De facto and tipping-point analyses gave similar results.
key_findings.locator: Table 5 (p. 27); 3.2.1.2.1 Primary Efficacy Endpoint, 2nd and 4th paragraphs (pp. 27-28)

key_findings.finding: In MAPP1 the between-arm difference appeared to grow over the three assessments; in MAPP2 it appeared similar at weeks 10 and 18 (Figure 2; numbers assessed printed under the figure: MAPP1 placebo 44, 43, 39, 37 and MDMA 46, 46, 42, 42 from baseline to week 18; MAPP2 placebo 50, 50, 44, 42 and MDMA 53, 53, 53, 52).
key_findings.locator: 3.2.1.2.1, 3rd paragraph; Figure 2 (rendered page; curve values not extracted)

key_findings.finding: Key secondary SDS (de jure, mITT): MAPP1 -3.15 vs -1.79, difference -1.36 (95% CI -2.46 to -0.25), P = 0.0167; MAPP2 -3.31 vs -2.11, difference -1.20 (-2.26 to -0.14), P = 0.0271; baseline means 6.8 and 7.4 (MAPP1), 6.0 and 6.1 (MAPP2).
key_findings.locator: 3.2.1.2.2 Secondary Efficacy Endpoint, 2nd paragraph; Table 6
key_findings.note: The published MAPP1 report gives P = 0.0116 for the SDS (card sc_mitchell_2021); the FDA's table, from the clinical study report, gives 0.0167. See reporting issue 6.

key_findings.finding: The FDA judges that MPLONG was "not properly planned, designed, and implemented to evaluate durability of treatment effect"; some participants sought other treatments in the interval, and functional unblinding, about 25% dropout and a single visit after a long and variable interval leave the results of very limited value.
key_findings.locator: 3.2.2.1 Populations and Baseline Characteristics for MPLONG, 1st paragraph

key_findings.finding: MPLONG enrolled 142 of the MAPP1 and MAPP2 participants: 30 (65.2% of those treated) from MAPP1's MDMA arm, 30 (68.2%) from its placebo arm, 45 (84.9%) from MAPP2's MDMA arm and 37 (72.5%) from its placebo arm; 137 were assessed, 62% (56 of 91) of those randomized in MAPP1 and 78% (81 of 104) in MAPP2. Those who enrolled had lower CAPS-5 at the end of the parent trial than those who did not (20.2 vs 30.9; MDMA arms 15.9 vs 25.4, placebo arms 24.9 vs 35.8) and lower baseline scores (40.6 vs 43.8).
key_findings.locator: 3.2.2.1, 2nd paragraph (p. 30); Table 7 (pp. 30-31)

key_findings.finding: Between the trials and the follow-up visit, of 151 people entering MPLONG from MAPP1, MAPP2 or MP16, 75 (82.4%) of those given MDMA and 43 (71.7%) of those given placebo had psychotherapy (psychodynamic, group, CBT, EMDR, prolonged exposure, cognitive processing, interpersonal); 12 MAPP1 or MAPP2 participants (6 from each arm) had ketamine-assisted psychotherapy and one placebo participant 5-MeO-DMT; 13 from the MDMA arms and 7 from the placebo arms reported using MDMA obtained outside the study; unreported use is possible.
key_findings.locator: 3.2.2.2 Interim Interventions between MAPP1, MAPP2 and MPLONG, 1st to 3rd paragraphs
key_findings.note: The denominators for 82.4% and 71.7% are not printed; they imply about 91 and 60 (editors' back-calculation).

key_findings.finding: MPLONG effectiveness subset (Table 8): least-squares mean CAPS-5 change from parent baseline at week 18 and at the follow-up visit: MAPP1 MDMA (n 27) -24.80 then -30.31, placebo (n 29) -15.96 then -15.61; MAPP2 MDMA (n 44) -24.41 then -28.01, placebo (n 37) -15.36 then -16.05. Change from week 18 to the visit: MAPP1 -5.51 (95% CI -9.95 to -1.07) on MDMA and +0.34 (-3.90 to 4.59) on placebo; MAPP2 -3.60 (-6.10 to -1.09) and -0.69 (-3.43 to 2.05). Raw follow-up means 12.7 vs 27.4 (MAPP1) and 11.3 vs 22.5 (MAPP2).
key_findings.locator: Table 8
key_findings.note: Editors' calculation from Table 8: between-arm differences of least-squares means 8.8 (MAPP1) and 9.0 (MAPP2) at week 18 in this subset, 14.7 and 12.0 at the follow-up visit; the FDA prints the latter two (p. 66) without intervals.

key_findings.finding: Median time from the last treatment to the follow-up visit: 23.4 months (range 7.9 to 32.4) for MAPP1 participants and 8.5 months (6.0 to 22.8) for MAPP2 participants.
key_findings.locator: 3.2.2.3 Exploratory Efficacy Assessments in Participants from MAPP1 and MAPP2, 2nd paragraph

key_findings.finding: An exploratory split by interval found no meaningful difference between people assessed 6 to 12 months and more than 12 months after the trial (mostly MAPP2 and MAPP1 respectively). In the FDA's tipping-point analysis, treating scores after interim ketamine, 5-MeO-DMT or MDMA use as missing and imputing them in the mITT population, the further improvement on MDMA from week 18 to the visit was -2.02 (95% CI -4.61 to 0.57) in MAPP2 and -4.93 (-9.32 to -0.53) in MAPP1, shrinking as imputed values were penalized; MAPP2 participants with such use improved more than those without, which was not seen in MAPP1.
key_findings.locator: 3.2.2.3, 3rd to 5th paragraphs (pp. 33-34); Tables 16 and 17 (pp. 70-71)

key_findings.finding: The FDA accepts a CAPS-5 change of 10 points or more as clinically meaningful, citing a systematic review (Varker et al., 2020) and its own review of the scale.
key_findings.locator: 3.2.3 Efficacy Issues in Detail › Efficacy Issue #1, 2nd paragraph

key_findings.finding: Functional unblinding may feed expectation bias (benefit expected on drug, disappointment on placebo); participants on MDMA guessed with more certainty (I think 15.4%, I am positive 78.8%) than those on placebo (31.8% and 43.2%), suggesting the bias may be imbalanced between arms.
key_findings.locator: Efficacy Issue #1, 3rd paragraph

key_findings.finding: In phase 2, low-dose MDMA comparators had been associated with anxiety and difficult sessions: in one study five participants in the low-dose group had higher CAPS scores after treatment, and in another seven low-dose participants improved less than eight placebo participants of another study with the same therapy team; the FDA and the sponsor then agreed on inactive placebo knowing the design may be susceptible to functional unblinding.
key_findings.locator: Efficacy Issue #1, 4th paragraph

key_findings.finding: MAPP2 blinding survey at study termination (Table 9, safety set): of 52 respondents on MDMA, 41 (78.8%) were positive and 8 (15.4%) thought they had the drug, 2 (3.8%) could not tell, 1 (1.9%) was positive they had placebo; of 44 respondents on placebo, 19 (43.2%) were positive and 14 (31.8%) thought they had placebo, 2 (4.5%) could not tell and 9 believed they had the drug (2 positive, 7 thought). Reasons on MDMA: positive mental or emotional effect 45 (86.5%), positive physical effect 29 (55.8%); on placebo: no effects 28 (63.6%).
key_findings.locator: Table 9

key_findings.finding: The placebo arms improved despite most knowing their allocation, so disappointment did not seem to worsen PTSD; but 94% of those given MDMA knew or thought they had it, so expectation bias could have acted more on the MDMA arm; its contribution remains difficult to quantify and may remain a factor in the drug-placebo difference.
key_findings.locator: Efficacy Issue #1, 6th and 7th paragraphs

key_findings.finding: The between-arm difference persisted into MPLONG for at least 6 months and in some cases more than a year; it is unclear how long expectation bias lasts in a chronic illness; the apparent durability might suggest a true drug effect, but dropouts, variable follow-up times and interim treatments are major limitations. In summary, two positive trials appear to show clinically meaningful effects whose interpretation is challenging because of likely functional unblinding and expectation bias, and the follow-up is likely affected by the same biases.
key_findings.locator: Efficacy Issue #1, 8th and 9th paragraphs

key_findings.finding: Durability concerns: a single visit at a variable time may not represent long-term symptom control; MAPP1 participants were unblinded before MPLONG; MPLONG began in March 2021, so MAPP1 participants waited longer; enrolment was self-selected and could be more stable people in either arm; those who enrolled had lower CAPS-5 at the end of the trials; and people who sought further treatment may have had less durable effects, which the tipping-point analysis seems consistent with.
key_findings.locator: Efficacy Issue #2: Durability of Treatment Effect, 1st to 9th paragraphs

key_findings.finding: The necessity of psychotherapy was assumed: there are no data on MDMA without psychotherapy or on the psychotherapy compared with no treatment; the MAPS manual gives broad guidelines and leaves therapists considerable flexibility, so the difference between arms suggests MDMA adds an effect but says nothing on whether the psychotherapy contributes independently.
key_findings.locator: Efficacy Issue #3: Contribution of Psychotherapy to Efficacy, 2nd and 3rd paragraphs

key_findings.finding: Safety database: 426 people exposed to MDMA in the sponsor's trials plus 50 in NIDA studies (476); treatment-emergent adverse events analysed in the pooled MAPP1 and MAPP2 set of 99 on MDMA and 95 on placebo; no pre- or post-dose laboratory tests in phase 3.
key_findings.locator: 3.3.1 Sources of Data for Safety, 1st to 3rd paragraphs

key_findings.finding: Two deaths in the programme, both in phase 2 from relapse of a previously diagnosed cancer more than 6 months after the last dose, judged unrelated. In MAPP1 three serious adverse events in two placebo participants (suicidal ideation; two suicide attempts by one participant on days 12 and 83); none in MAPP2. Across the programme one serious event was judged probably related to MDMA: ventricular extrasystoles in a phase 2 participant (MP-8) with pre-existing ectopy, hospitalized for monitoring. Discontinuation for adverse events: one MDMA participant (depression) against placebo participants with abdominal pain, insomnia, panic attack, suicidal ideation (2) and suicide attempts.
key_findings.locator: 3.3.2.1 Deaths; 3.3.2.2 Serious Adverse Events; Tables 10 to 12

key_findings.finding: Pooled adverse events in at least 2% on MDMA and more often than on placebo (Table 13; MDMA n = 99, placebo n = 95): headache 71.7% vs 57.9%; bruxism and jaw tightness (events of jaw tension, tightness, clenching, grinding or stiffness grouped together) 57.6% vs 14.7%; decreased appetite 43.4% vs 10.5%; insomnia 39.4% vs 29.5%; nausea 38.4% vs 16.8%; fatigue 28.3% vs 24.2%; hyperhidrosis 28.3% vs 4.2%; dizziness 24.2% vs 13.7%; muscle tightness other than the jaw 21.2% vs 9.5%; feeling cold 20.2% vs 6.3%; restlessness 15.2% vs 2.1%; mydriasis 13.1% vs 0; nystagmus 13.1% vs 1.1%; feeling jittery 13.1% vs 0; blurred vision 12.1% vs 1.1%; palpitations 9.1% vs 7.4%; blood pressure increased 7.1% vs 0; intrusive thoughts 6.1% vs 0; substance use 3.0% vs 0; binge drinking 2.0% vs 0.
key_findings.locator: 3.3.2.4 Frequent AEs in the Phase 3 Studies; Table 13 and its footnotes

key_findings.finding: Blood pressure and heart rate were recorded only at 0955 (dosing at 1000), at 1130 (when the supplemental dose was given if tolerated) and at 1730, the close of the session. In the pooled sets 46% on MDMA vs 17% on placebo had a systolic rise of 20 mm Hg or more in the third session, and 45% vs 32% a diastolic rise of 10 mm Hg or more; mean rises of 17 mm Hg systolic and 7 mm Hg diastolic and of 23 beats per minute after session 3; pulse stayed about 10 beats above predose at the session's end.
key_findings.locator: Adverse Events of Special Interest, item 1 (a and b)
key_findings.note: Figure 4 (p. 45, rendered) shows the placebo-corrected rises largest at the interim measurement and smaller at the endpoint; values not extracted.

key_findings.finding: Vital-sign outliers (Table 14): systolic 140 mm Hg or more 67 of 99 (67.7%) vs 21 of 95 (22.1%), risk difference 45.6 (95% CI 33.1 to 58.0); 160 or more 33.3% vs 4.2%; 180 or more 6 of 99 (6.1%) vs 0, 6.1 (1.4 to 10.8); a rise of 40 or more over baseline 13.1% vs 1.1%; diastolic 100 mm Hg or more 29.3% vs 8.4%; heart rate 110 or more and at least 10 above baseline 23 of 99 (23.2%) vs 0. The FDA considers severe hypertension most relevant to cardiovascular events because exposure is intermittent.
key_findings.locator: Adverse Events of Special Interest, item 1, last bullet (p. 45); Table 14 (pp. 45-46)

key_findings.finding: Only one cardiac arrhythmia occurred in the programme (the MP-8 serious event), but there were no scheduled post-dose ECGs in phase 2 or 3, and the sponsor's literature search on arrhythmia was not exhaustive. Effects considered neutral, positive or favourable were not systematically recorded.
key_findings.locator: Adverse Events of Special Interest, items 2 and 3

key_findings.finding: Suicidality (pooled): suicidal-ideation events of special interest rated mild or moderate in 40 (40%) on MDMA and 41 (43%) on placebo; the two rated severe were both in MAPP1's placebo arm; a rise from a C-SSRS of 3 or less to 4 or 5 in 4 of 98 (4.1%) vs 3 of 93 (3.2%); no new suicidal behaviour in people without a history of it, and no pattern in the 24 to 72 hours after sessions.
key_findings.locator: Adverse Events of Special Interest, item 4

key_findings.finding: Other psychiatric events more frequent on MDMA: anxiety, restlessness, bruxism, nightmare, intrusive thoughts, nervousness, flashbacks, insomnia and sleep disorder, several of them PTSD symptoms and some possibly stimulant effects. Thermoregulatory events (feeling cold or hot, chills) and osmoregulatory events (hyperhidrosis, thirst, cold sweat) were more frequent on MDMA without meaningful temperature changes; their significance is unclear.
key_findings.locator: Adverse Events of Special Interest, items 5 and 6

key_findings.finding: Liver function was tested only in MP-1 (23 participants), MP-2 (14) and MPKF (16), with abnormal results in nine across the three and one shift from normal to high (AST 43); for MAPP1 and MAPP2 the submitted laboratory file holds only the drug screen, hepatitis C, pregnancy test, C-reactive protein and carotid ultrasound, other screening tests remaining in site records not entered into the data file; no haematology, electrolytes, renal or liver tests on dosing days.
key_findings.locator: Adverse Events of Special Interest, item 7; 3.3.3.1 › Clinical Laboratory Data are Limited, 1st to 3rd paragraphs

key_findings.finding: Against the ICH E1A exposure guideline (1,500 people, 300 to 600 for 6 months, 100 for a year), the FDA judges that it would not apply to a three-session regimen for a serious condition, so the database of 476 may be adequate if the regimen is supported.
key_findings.locator: 3.3.3.1 › Size of the Safety Database, 2nd paragraph

key_findings.finding: Data on intrinsic arrhythmia risk are inadequate under the 2012 QT guidance and confounded by the rise in heart rate; whether MDMA has intrinsic or conditional proarrhythmic potential is unclear. The combined rise in heart rate and systolic pressure raises the rate-pressure product, a predictor of ischaemic events; no major cardiovascular event occurred in a limited database.
key_findings.locator: 3.3.3.1 › Cardiovascular Safety, 1st to 3rd paragraphs

key_findings.finding: Despite the FDA's advice of 9 March 2017 that abuse-related adverse events be documented in all studies, the application states that effects considered neutral, positive or favourable by the participant, therapist and study physician were not systematically collected as adverse events; such effects were first collected in the open-label MAPPUSX in 2023; the FDA says this approach "inherently underrepresents the range and frequency of CNS AEs" in the trials.
key_findings.locator: 3.3.3.1 › Midomafetamine Effects Perceived as Positive Were Not Recorded, 1st to 4th paragraphs

key_findings.finding: Abuse potential (the FDA's regulatory term): published animal studies consistently show rewarding effects (self-administration, conditioned place preference, drug discrimination with both stimulants and psychedelics); the sponsor ran no human abuse-potential study, and in the published studies MDMA produced similar or greater drug liking than amphetamine, methamphetamine or methylphenidate, in people with and without prior MDMA use, so the FDA concludes its abuse potential is equal to or greater than these Schedule II comparators.
key_findings.locator: 3.3.4.1 Abuse Potential Assessments in Animals; 3.3.4.2.1 Human Abuse Potential Studies; Conclusions From the Clinical Abuse Potential Literature Review

key_findings.finding: The FDA states that excluding positive effects was not consistent with its 2017 advice and that the sponsor thereby excluded most of the events used in an abuse-potential evaluation. In MAPPUSX, among participants dosed after 23 February 2023, relaxation was recorded in 8 (18.6%), euphoric mood in 3 (7%), derealization and altered time perception in 2 each (4.7%); despite the limited collection, the FDA reads these events as a clear signal of abuse potential.
key_findings.locator: 3.3.4.2.2 Abuse-Related Adverse Events From Applicant's Clinical Studies, the two paragraphs after the quoted 2017 advice; Table 15

key_findings.finding: Illicit MDMA (FDA's independent analyses): past-year nonmedical use generally 1% or less; 7,614 abuse-related poison-centre cases involving MDMA in 2012 to 2022, fatal in 0.7% (methamphetamine 8.2%), major outcomes in 10.4% of single-substance MDMA cases (amphetamines 5.0%, methylphenidate 2.9%); 693 MDMA-involved overdose deaths in 2010 to 2017 (methamphetamine 33,505) and 882 in 35 states and DC in 2019 to 2022, only 7.3% single-substance. The FDA lists harms in the literature that the sponsor's proposed label did not address (myocardial infarction, cerebral haemorrhage, aortic dissection, arrhythmias, respiratory events, liver injury, neuropsychiatric events) and cases where MDMA was used to perpetrate sexual assault, with the caveats of polysubstance use and unknown purity.
key_findings.locator: 3.3.5 Epidemiologic Data on Patterns of Use and Harms Associated with Illicit MDMA

key_findings.finding: In the trials MDMA was given under medical supervision with two therapists for 8 hours in a controlled setting, most participants also staying overnight; participants agreed not to drive until the next day; discharge followed no clear objective criteria and was left to the therapists; onset, duration and nature of the short-term effects were not captured.
key_findings.locator: 3.4 Risk Mitigation, 2nd and 3rd paragraphs

key_findings.finding: Proposed REMS if approved: dispensing only in certified healthcare settings, documented safe-use conditions, monitoring of every patient by at least two healthcare providers (one licensed) for at least 8 hours and until stable, release to an accompanying adult, follow-up after each session and a patient registry; a postmarketing requirement and enhanced pharmacovigilance are considered because of the small database, limited data and unrecorded positive effects.
key_findings.locator: Agency's Proposed REMS, 1st to 6th paragraphs; Postmarketing

key_findings.finding: Pre-decisional benefit-risk framework: both trials positive on CAPS-5 and SDS and considered clinically meaningful; effectiveness if the results could be taken at face value; functional unblinding with around 80 to 90% of the MDMA arm guessing correctly; in MPLONG a similar difference from placebo maintained (-14.7 in MAPP1, -11.96 in MAPP2) and continued improvement in every arm except MAPP1's placebo arm, though confounded; therapy not standardized across the trials; impairment of at least 8 hours with no data on discharge criteria; cardiovascular risk not determinable in a small database; no suicidality signal; abuse-potential signals similar to Schedule II comparators; the sponsor had not documented CNS adverse events, in particular positive ones such as euphoria, as the Controlled Substance Staff had advised.
key_findings.locator: Benefit-Risk Framework: Benefits row and Risks and Risk Management row, both columns

key_findings.finding: Scoping review of illicit MDMA harms: PubMed and Embase searched on 18 January 2024 for 2008 to 2024; two reviewers screened 4,273 records; 235 epidemiological and 100 case-report articles abstracted; 92 English-language case articles with 124 cases coded to MedDRA.
key_findings.locator: 6.2.4 Scoping Literature Review

reporting_issues.issue: The MAPP2 survey result for the MDMA arm is given as about 90% (p. 8), 94% (p. 36) and around 80 to 90% (p. 66); Table 9 (p. 35) gives 49 of 52 (94.2%).
reporting_issues.consequence: Cite Table 9; the summary figures understate the unblinding on MDMA.

reporting_issues.issue: The text says a higher proportion enrolled in MPLONG from MAPP2's placebo arm than from its MDMA arm (85% and 73%); the FDA's own figures on p. 30 give 84.9% for the MDMA arm (45 of 53) and 72.5% for placebo (37 of 51): the arms are swapped.
reporting_issues.consequence: Use p. 30: more of the MDMA arm than of the placebo arm enrolled in MAPP2.

reporting_issues.issue: The follow-up interval is given as 6 to 24 months after parent-study completion (p. 25) but as up to 32.4 months after the last treatment for MAPP1 (p. 32), and as 6 months to more than 2 years elsewhere (pp. 9, 24).
reporting_issues.consequence: Cite the medians and ranges on p. 32.

reporting_issues.issue: Table 8 labels the bracketed values beside the least-squares mean changes as SE, but each is a pair of numbers, an interval; its footnote lists visits 13, 15 and 19 in the model, while the methods (p. 24) name visits 8, 13 and 19 (visit 15 is a medication session).
reporting_issues.consequence: Read the pairs as 95% intervals; the model's visits cannot be confirmed.

reporting_issues.issue: The SDS is described as a total of three items scored 0 to 10 (range 0 to 30), but Table 6 prints baseline means of 6.0 to 7.4 and week-18 means of 2.7 to 5.3, values that fit a 0 to 10 metric (editors' inference).
reporting_issues.consequence: The SDS differences of 1.2 and 1.36 should be read on the 0 to 10 metric the trial reports use, not as points of a 0 to 30 total.

reporting_issues.issue: Table 6 gives P = 0.0167 for MAPP1's SDS difference (from the clinical study report), whereas the published MAPP1 report gives P = 0.0116 (card sc_mitchell_2021).
reporting_issues.consequence: A discrepancy between the regulator's table and the publication; the difference remains significant in both.

reporting_issues.issue: Collection of positive or neutral effects in MAPPUSX is said to begin on 15 March 2023 (p. 50) and on 23 February 2023 (p. 56, Table 15).
reporting_issues.consequence: Date uncertain to within three weeks; it does not affect the finding that the controlled trials did not collect them.

reporting_issues.issue: The text lists one hallucination and one intentional product misuse among the MAPPUSX abuse-related events, but Table 15 lists derealization, altered time perception and abnormal thinking and neither of those two terms.
reporting_issues.consequence: The misuse event is stated in the text only; cite it as such.

reporting_issues.issue: Anxiety is named among events more frequent on MDMA (p. 47) but has no row in Table 13, which lists every term in at least 2% on MDMA and more frequent than placebo; bruxism is named there as psychiatric but tabulated as musculoskeletal.
reporting_issues.consequence: Do not cite an excess of anxiety on MDMA from this document.

reporting_issues.issue: The text gives blood pressure at or above 140/90 mm Hg in 68% vs 22% (risk difference 45.6), but these are Table 14's figures for systolic pressure of 140 or more alone; diastolic 90 or more was 68.7% vs 34.7%. The text says systolic above 180 where the table says 180 or more.
The alcohol and cannabis use disorder exclusion excludes moderate disorder within the past 3 months, while its parenthetical note says moderate disorder in the 3 months before enrolment was allowed.
reporting_issues.consequence: The exact eligibility for people with alcohol or cannabis use disorder cannot be read from this document.

reporting_issues.issue: The benefit-risk framework says each medication session was bracketed by 1 preparatory and 3 integrative sessions, whereas the study description gives three preparatory sessions before the first medication session.
reporting_issues.consequence: Use the study description (three preparatory sessions in all).

reporting_issues.issue: Before the erratum, the document called the CAPS-5 a 20-item measure, allocated 2% (rather than 0.2%) of alpha to the sample-size re-estimation, described MPLONG as enrolling only people given MDMA and as reviewing adverse events, and restricted the ecstasy-use exclusion to MAPP2; 24 table and figure cross-references were blank.

verification.source_read: PDF pp. 1-83 (PDFs/MDMA/FDA_2024_BriefingDocument.pdf), read in full from the text layer (pdftotext -layout); pp. 21, 26-29, 32-33, 35-36, 42-46 and 70 rendered at 110 dpi and checked (Tables 2-6, 8, 9, 13, 14, 16 and Figures 1-4); read together with the erratum (fda_2024b).
